newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah little changed in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah little changed in late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was little changed against the dollar in dull late trading on Tuesday.
Dealers said volume was thin, with ample rupiah supply seen softening swap rates across the board.
One local bank dealer said there were some commercial dollar buying orders in the afternoon but steady supply by some state banks kept the dollar-rupiah rate stable.
One Japanese bank dealer said there were also some purchases by London operators which helped the dollar edge up slightly. He said ample liquidity had also made it possible.
Spot rupiah was at 2,385.5/86.0 at 0900 GMT against an opening of 2,384.5/85.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,385.00/85.35 and 2,384.4/84.8, respectively.

The dealer said liquidity remained the underlying issue. He said some operators seemed to view the present excess supply as only temporary because the approaching fiscal year end on March 31 would drain rupiah due to higher tax payments.
Overnight rupiah closed at eight percent, recovering from 5.5 percent after the central bank offered bilateral papers.
One-month swaps edged down to 10.75/11.25 from 11.5/12.5, two to 24.75/26.00 from 25.5/26.5, three to 37.5/39.0 from 38.5/39.0 and six to 77.0/77.5 from 78.0/78.5 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,379/2,571 and the conversion band also by one point to 2,379/2,427 on Tuesday.
The bank depreciated the rupiah by two points last week, after lowering it by four points the previous week.
